chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj who said:

A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who commanded his slave to perform Tamattu' (combining Hajj and 'Umrah), and he said: 'Command him to fast, and if you wish, slaughter an animal on his behalf.'
ai.seo_question: What is the compensation if a slave fails to fast during Tamattu' pilgrimage?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the compensation (kaffarah) for a slave who performs Tamattu' but fails to fast, offering the master the choice between commanding the slave to fast or slaughtering a sacrificial animal on his behalf. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the obligations of slaves versus free persons, acknowledging the slave's limited autonomy while ensuring the ritual validity of the pilgrimage. The option to slaughter an animal serves as a practical alternative when the slave is unable or unwilling to fast, reflecting the compassionate legal principles applied to different social classes in early Islamic society.
